subject: reasoning
question: M, N, O, P, Y and Z live on six different floors of the same building. The lowermost floor in the building is numbered 1, the floor above it, number 2 and so on till the topmost floor is numbered 6. Only two people live between O and Z. Only two people live between N and M. Only one person lives between P and M. P lives on floor numbered 1. O lives above M. How many people live below Y?
solution:
Given: M, N, O, P, Y and Z live on six different floors of the same building. The lowermost floor in the building is numbered 1, the floor above it, number 2 and so on till the topmost floor is numbered 6.

1) P lives on floor numbered 1.

2) Only one person lives between P and M.

3) Only two people live between N and M.

4) Only two people live between O and Z. Also, O lives above M.**
Possible positions for O and Z:

 
• If O is on Floor 5, then Z is on Floor 2 (two people, M and the person on Floor 4, are between them).
 
• If O is on Floor 4, then Z would need to be on Floor 1, but P is already there. So this is not possible.

Therefore, O is on Floor 5 and Z is on Floor 2.

5) The only remaining person is Y, and the only remaining floor is 4. So, Y lives on Floor 4.

Therefore, three** people live below Y.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 3"**.
